songs.name: He Was A Friend Of Mine

ai_show_review.summary: High‑energy early set with Golden Road into New Potato and a fiery Alligator jam
ai_show_review.blurb: Features a concise four‑song set that rides high energy from The Golden Road into New Potato Caboose and rolls straight into an organ‑driven Alligator. Jerry delivers a scorching solo on He Was A Friend Of Mine while Pigpen’s B3 adds texture throughout.
ai_show_review.review: May 5, 1967 at the Fillmore Auditorium finds the Dead in full teenage swagger, launching a tight four‑song set that still feels fresh to modern ears. The band launches with The Golden Road [To Unlimited Devotion], a bright, riff‑driven opener that seamlessly segues into New Potato Caboose; the transition is effortless and showcases their early knack for flowing between songs. Alligator follows, turning into an organ‑heavy jam where Pigpen’s whizzing B3 takes center stage, while Phil’s bass punches through the mix and Bill (Billy) keeps a solid groove despite a slightly muddy low end. The set closes with He Was A Friend Of Mine, giving Jerry a chance to stretch out on a soulful solo that caps the night with genuine feeling. Across three soundboard sources the performance is consistently high‑energy, with the yerys tape offering the clearest instrument separation and the Wolfe‑Smith masters providing an excellent, crystal‑clear picture of this rare 1967 gem.

best_recording.reason: Good‑quality soundboard with clear instrument separation; captures the full four‑song set and the high‑energy flow of the night.

key_highlights: Fiery performance of The Golden Road into New Potato Caboose with seamless segue
Alligator jam highlighted by Pigpen’s whizzing B3 organ and Phil’s hot bass lines
Jerry’s powerful solo on He Was A Friend Of Mine
Early Jimi‑Hendrix‑inspired vibe that hints at the band’s developing psychedelic edge
song_highlights: He Was A Friend Of Mine

band_performance.Jerry: Fiery, on‑point guitar work with a scorching solo on He Was A Friend Of Mine; early Gibson tone feels loose and free.
band_performance.Phil: Hot, prominent bass lines that drive the Alligator jam; described as ‘having a ball’ throughout the set.
band_performance.Bob: Strong three‑part vocal harmonies with Jerry and Phil and solid rhythm guitar underpinning the songs.
band_performance.Pigpen: Whizzing B3 organ adds rich texture, especially in the Alligator jam where it becomes a focal point.
band_performance.Billy: Solid, artistic drumming that propels the set; occasional low‑end mud but overall tight and driving.
